item.title: Secretary Rubio’s Meeting with Philippine President Marcos
item.dc:creator: Office of the Spokesperson
item.description:
Office of the Spokesperson

Secretary Rubio’s Meeting with Philippine President Marcos

Readout

July 22, 2026

The below is attributable to Spokesperson Tommy Pigott:

Secretary of State Marco Rubio met in Manila with President Ferdinand Marcos, Jr. of the Philippines to reaffirm our ironclad Alliance and our shared commitment to a free and open Indo-Pacific.  They underscored the importance of upholding freedoms of navigation and overflight in the South China Sea and noted the recent tenth anniversary of the July 2016 Arbitral Award in the South China Sea, confirming that there is no legal basis for China’s expansive maritime claims in the South China Sea.

They also discussed advancing the Luzon Economic Corridor, most notably the Department of State’s commitment, working with Congress, to deliver over $100 million dollars of new foreign assistance to upgrade infrastructure and advance logistics and energy projects in Subic, as well as the upcoming inaugural Luzon Economic Corridor Investment Forum in September.

Secretary Rubio and President Marcos also discussed opportunities related to the Philippines’ membership in Pax Silica and hosting the initiative’s first Economic Security Zone in Clark.  Secretary Rubio hailed the deployment of the Expeditionary Cutter Squadron that will operate from forward locations in Singapore and the Philippines to enhance maritime interoperability and support shared regional security objectives. 

Through the five-year, jointly funded Health Strategic Objective Agreement, they also reaffirmed shared commitments to preventing the spread of infectious diseases, improving health outcomes, and building a more resilient and sustainable health system in the Philippines.

item.title: United States-Republic of Korea (ROK)-Japan Trilateral Foreign Ministers’ Meeting
item.dc:creator: Office of the Spokesperson
item.description:
Office of the Spokesperson

United States-Republic of Korea (ROK)-Japan Trilateral Foreign Ministers’ Meeting

Readout

July 22, 2026

The below is attributable to Spokesperson Tommy Pigott: 

Secretary of State Marco Rubio met today with ROK Foreign Minister Cho Hyun and Japanese Foreign Minister Motegi Toshimitsu on the margins of the ASEAN Foreign Ministers Meetings in Manila.  The Secretary and his counterparts emphasized the importance of working with ASEAN on issues of mutual interest, including strengthening defense cooperation and maritime security, advancing energy security, combatting cyber threats, and promoting peace and stability across Southeast Asia and the broader Indo-Pacific.

The Secretary and Foreign Ministers committed to intensifying joint efforts targeting transnational criminal organizations, including networks operating scam centers that defraud and endanger citizens across the region.  They committed to expanding trilateral discussions on Arctic issues, recognizing the region’s growing strategic importance.  They also reaffirmed commitments to defense cooperation, maritime security, and upholding freedom of navigation, and pledged continued trilateral consultations at all levels.

The Secretary and Foreign Ministers reaffirmed the importance of maintaining a unified approach toward the Democratic People’s Republic of Korea (DPRK), underscoring their shared commitment to the complete denuclearization of the DPRK and continued coordination to counter DPRK cyber threats and illicit activity as well as to the immediate resolution of the abductions issue.  They also emphasized the importance of maintaining peace and stability across the Taiwan Strait.  The Secretary and Foreign Ministers noted with concern China’s lack of sufficient notification of their recent intercontinental ballistic missile launch into the Pacific Ocean. 

The Secretary and Foreign Ministers discussed next steps to implement the trilateral Memorandum of Cooperation on Small Modular Reactor Deployments in Other Countries signed in Ankara and to start deployment in the Indo-Pacific to advance energy diversification and technology cooperation.  They also underscored the importance of economic security, reaffirmed shared opposition to economic coercion and the weaponization of supply chains, and committed to derisking and diversifying critical supply chains and to further trusted technology cooperation.

item.title: Secretary Rubio’s Meeting with Indian External Affairs Minister Jaishankar
item.dc:creator: Office of the Spokesperson
item.description:
Office of the Spokesperson

Secretary Rubio’s Meeting with Indian External Affairs Minister Jaishankar

Readout

July 22, 2026

The below is attributable to Spokesperson Tommy Pigott:

Secretary Rubio met today with Indian External Affairs Minister Jaishankar in Manila.  The Secretary and Minister Jaishankar discussed recent developments in the Middle East and the Indo-Pacific.

The Secretary and Minister Jaishankar discussed finalizing key defense agreements in fulfillment of commitments made between President Trump and Prime Minister Modi last year.

The Secretary and Minister Jaishankar agreed on the importance of finalizing the interim trade deal, which is almost complete.

item.title: Joint Statement on Cooperation with ASEAN by the Quad Foreign Ministers
item.dc:creator: Office of the Spokesperson
item.description:
Office of the Spokesperson

Joint Statement on Cooperation with ASEAN by the Quad Foreign Ministers

Media Note

July 22, 2026

The text of the following statement was released by the Secretary of State of the United States, the Foreign Minister of Australia, the External Affairs Minister of India, and the Foreign Minister of Japan.  

Begin text:  

As ASEAN Comprehensive Strategic Partners, we, the Secretary of State of the United States and the Foreign Ministers of Australia, India, and Japan, met today in Manila to reaffirm our commitment to strengthening a free and open Indo-Pacific and our unwavering support for ASEAN unity and centrality. 

We are deeply invested in the region’s success and in cooperating with ASEAN and its member states. 

We discussed regional challenges and opportunities to strengthen our support for the practical implementation of the ASEAN Outlook on the Indo-Pacific (AOIP) through our shared priorities of maritime and transnational security, economic prosperity and security, critical and emerging technologies, and humanitarian assistance and emergency response. 

We are united in our conviction that peace and stability in the Indo-Pacific maritime domain underpin the security and prosperity of the region. 

End text.

item.title: Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos, Jr. Before Their Meeting
item.dc:creator: Marco Rubio, Secretary of State
item.description:
Marco Rubio, Secretary of State

Manila, Philippines

Malacañan Palace

Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos, Jr. Before Their Meeting

Remarks

July 22, 2026

PRESIDENT MARCOS:  (Inaudible) welcome you to the Malacañan Palace in Manila.  (Inaudible) and we know that you have a very, very busy schedule, a lot of important things you are doing, that you have found the time for this (inaudible), especially as (inaudible) chair of ASEAN.  I really appreciate (inaudible) many issues that (inaudible).  I’m very glad, as I mentioned to you, we watch the news and so we were surprised that you are still able to find time to visit with us (inaudible).  Thank you very much (inaudible). 

SECRETARY RUBIO:  Well, thank you for welcoming me, first of all, and to congratulate you on the great job hosting this conference, which, in addition to being so critically important for the region, provides us the opportunity to interact with so many countries.  It’s also important to be here I think just two weeks into our new ambassador here, who I know is going to do a great job.  And Mr. President, thank you for welcoming us.  And obviously, in addition to visiting here for the conference, we wanted to visit with you. You know how much the President holds you in high esteem; you had a very positive meeting last year in Washington.  And this is a country that has deep ties to the United States in many ways and it’s a partnership that is only growing, and in light of recent events, it’s become more important than ever.  And so we’re glad to be with you today and to reaffirm that relationship and our commitment to the U.S. and Philippines’ relationship.

item.title: Secretary of State Marco Rubio at the ASEAN Post-Ministerial Conference with the United States
item.dc:creator: Marco Rubio, Secretary of State
item.description:
Marco Rubio, Secretary of State

Manila, Philippines

Philippine International Convention Center

Secretary of State Marco Rubio at the ASEAN Post-Ministerial Conference with the United States

Remarks

July 22, 2026

SECRETARY RUBIO:  Well, thank you.  First of all, let me thank you, my colleague from Cambodia, for being our country coordinator now for the second year, two years and running, and I think we’ve got one more together, and we appreciate very much all the work you put into this.  I also want to thank you, Mr. Secretary-General.  I appreciate very much all of the efforts that have gone into putting this on and involving us in this process.   

As President Trump stated last year at the leaders meeting, the U.S.-ASEAN, at the summit, we’re with ASEAN 100 percent.  This is the primary mechanism by which we engage the region, and you will continue to see our commitment to it at the highest levels, including with our ambassador, who recently came on board.  And in addition to our ambassador here in the host country – who, by the way, have done a phenomenal job; thank you for hosting us.  We’ve fallen in love with your country.  I visited here many years ago as a senator, but it’s so much more fun to visit as a Secretary of State.  But we appreciate that.  I know how much work goes into putting one of these on, and you’ve done a phenomenal job, and we thank you.   

Before we get into the other topics, I know there’s an area that’s on everyone’s mind, and it’s what’s occurring in the Middle East.  And I just want to reiterate once again, the United States is always committed to diplomacy. We are open-minded and always willing to engage in negotiated settlements of differences.  And that remains true in the case of Iran.  

Unfortunately, as of now, despite their direct outreaches – and Iran has been reaching out to the United States, both directly and indirectly, to engage in talks about settling the differences with regards to what’s happening in that part of the world.  Unfortunately, so far, even though we have reached agreements, they have not kept their commitments.  And as the President stated earlier today, I guess, yes, today Washington time, yesterday our time here now, the problem we’re having right now is that they’re not serious about talks.  If they’re serious, we’re serious.  If they’re not, then we will do what is necessary to protect that, our interests, and also the interests of our allies.   

At its core, it’s very simple.  Iran demands the right, which they do not have under any existing legal mechanism, to control the transit of traffic through the Straits of Hormuz.  This is an international waterway.  And of all the regions in the world, the one I don’t need to talk – teach about the importance of freedom of navigation in international waterways, it is this region.  And if we create a precedent in the Middle East where a nation state can decide that they are going to control an international waterway, charge a toll, and if you don’t pay them, blow up your ships, we have created a very dangerous precedent which will repeat itself in other parts of the world, including in this region.   

So what is at stake here is not simply the issue of what’s happening in the Straits of Hormuz.  It’s a very fundamental principle about freedom of navigation.  And if that is threatened, then I think the global economy is threatened and the rules which have underpinned 150 years of international trade and commerce are also threatened.  And that cannot be allowed to happen.   

But as I said, the United States remains open and willing to engage in positive, constructive negotiations and talks so long as the commitments that are made are kept.  And when those commitments are not kept, which is what’s happened in this particular case, then there will be consequences.  And that has to happen.  If these consequences did not exist, then today we would be living in a world where the significant percentage of the energy supply of this region and 20 percent of the energy supply of the world is being held hostage by a nation-state, by a rogue regime, who intends to appropriate that and the right of tolling and controlling that shipping to itself – a right they do not have under any definition of international laws, particularly those that govern maritime transit.   

Now, I want to talk briefly about our partnership here in this regard as well.  I’m proud to announce that the United States’ commitment is being evidenced – to ASEAN is being evidenced by action.  The United States is now going to, as we announced last year and have been following up in the year since our last gathering, leverage all available tools in our government to strengthen these relations, and that includes on the topic of foreign assistance.   

As part of that effort, we’re delivering $2.5 billion in U.S. Government strategic investments in Southeast Asia, reinforcing our commitment to the region, and we’re investing because the development of ASEAN is also in the interest of the United States.  This is not charity.  This is not something we’re doing because we’re nice people – although I believe we are nice people, but it’s in our national interest.  Our partnership with each of your countries and the region at large, it’s in the national interest of the United States, and we will never abandon it.  No matter what else is going on in the world, no matter what our bilateral relations may be with other countries, we’re a powerful country that has a global reach, and so we have to have relations with powerful countries with whom we have some disagreements.  But that will never come at the expense of our alliances, it will never come at the expense of our partners, and it will never come at the expense of our national interest.  And our relationship with each country represented here today is in our national interest.   

In addition, we are also seeking to leverage other financial tools available to our government to seek new opportunities within ASEAN.  The recent approval by the Development Finance Corporation to provide $1.5 billion in new strategic investments advancing aviation infrastructure, energy security, and secure supply chains is among the things we want to achieve together with all of you.   

As this region becomes the engine of economic growth in the 21st century – and I’ve said this with all due respect to other parts of the world that we also care about and are involved in – but I believe very much that the future and the story of the 21st century will be written in this region and by how events unfold here.  And the security and prosperity of the United States and Southeast Asia will always depend on each other.   

In ASEAN, as ASEAN develops its digital economy, diversifies its sources of energy, and builds a more secure supply chain, the United States wants to provide solutions to these regional issues.  We want to be among your featured and most trusted partners in each of these endeavors.  We’re committing to support security in the region through nearly $130 million in assistance to ASEAN countries for demining, which reflects our commitment to the safety of everyday citizens.  We recognize that pragmatism underpins programs and activities in ASEAN, and we want to support a safer and more secure Southeast Asia for your peoples.   

We’re also continuing to boost energy security in the region by supporting LNG market development, the deployment of U.S. grid technologies, and support to the ASEAN power grid, building safe, secure, and responsible civil nuclear energy programs and investing in regional energy infrastructure, including critical mineral supply chains.  As ASEAN seeks to implement its ASEAN Petroleum Security Agreement, the United States will continue to stay heavily engaged on energy-related issues.   

The United States, as I said earlier and I repeat again, stands with ASEAN, and we’re working together to strengthen our economies and our people through forward-looking collaboration that will ensure that the U.S. is your reliable and durable partner for the next 50 years and beyond.  So I look forward to our discussion today on the issues that will shape our comprehensive strategic partnership for the years to come.  Thank you.

item.title: United States and Catholic Relief Services Send First Humanitarian Flight to Cuba Under Secretary Rubio’s New $100 Million Assistance Commitment
item.dc:creator: Office of the Spokesperson
item.description:
Office of the Spokesperson

United States and Catholic Relief Services Send First Humanitarian Flight to Cuba Under Secretary Rubio’s New $100 Million Assistance Commitment

Media Note

July 21, 2026

Senior Official for Foreign Assistance, Humanitarian Affairs, and Religious Freedom Jeremy Lewin and Bureau of Western Hemisphere Affairs Senior Advisor Viviana Bovo joined Catholic Relief Services (CRS) in Miami, Florida, on July 21 to send off the first flight of humanitarian relief under Secretary Rubio’s historic commitment of $100 million in humanitarian assistance to the Cuban people, who are suffering from the consequences of the Communist regime’s kleptocracy, brutality, and economic incompetence.

This partnership builds upon the success of the Department’s program last year with CRS and Caritas Cuba to deliver $9 million in direct support to the island following Hurricane Melissa. Today’s flight contains pre-packaged food and hygiene kits for up to 700 Cuban families. The kits will be delivered by CRS, in partnership with the Catholic Church and Caritas Cuba on the ground. Building on the success of the previous program, the direct delivery of humanitarian commodities by local parish representatives in the island will ensure critical U.S. assistance reaches everyday Cubans in need, without any opportunity for regime diversion or theft.

Media Note

July 21, 2026

Senior Official for Foreign Assistance, Humanitarian Affairs, and Religious Freedom Jeremy Lewin and Bureau of Western Hemisphere Affairs Senior Advisor Viviana Bovo joined Catholic Relief Services (CRS) in Miami, Florida, on July 21 to send off the first flight of humanitarian relief under Secretary Rubio’s historic commitment of $100 million in humanitarian assistance to the Cuban people, who are suffering from the consequences of the Communist regime’s kleptocracy, brutality, and economic incompetence.

This partnership builds upon the success of the Department’s program last year with CRS and Caritas Cuba to deliver $9 million in direct support to the island following Hurricane Melissa. Today’s flight contains pre-packaged food and hygiene kits for up to 700 Cuban families. The kits will be delivered by CRS, in partnership with the Catholic Church and Caritas Cuba on the ground. Building on the success of the previous program, the direct delivery of humanitarian commodities by local parish representatives in the island will ensure critical U.S. assistance reaches everyday Cubans in need, without any opportunity for regime diversion or theft.

item.title: A Call to Action: Addressing the Murillo-Ortega Dictatorship’s Vow to Abolish Elections
item.dc:creator: Marco Rubio, Secretary of State
item.description:
Marco Rubio, Secretary of State

A Call to Action:  Addressing the Murillo-Ortega Dictatorship’s Vow to Abolish Elections

Press Statement

July 21, 2026

Daniel Ortega’s declaration that under his family’s dictatorship Nicaragua will never again hold elections lays bare their true authoritarian nature.  Daniel Ortega and Rosario Murillo have abandoned even the pretense of popular consent.

The Nicaraguan people have the right to choose their own leaders through democratic elections.  The United States calls on the international community to join forces to demonstrate to the Murillo-Ortega dictatorship that it cannot expect to maintain business as usual with other nations when it is thwarting the basic tenets of our democratic hemisphere.

item.title: Deputy Secretary Landau’s Meeting with Solomon Islands Prime Minister Wale
item.dc:creator: Office of the Spokesperson
item.description:
Office of the Spokesperson

Deputy Secretary Landau’s Meeting with Solomon Islands Prime Minister Wale

Readout

July 21, 2026

Deputy Secretary of State Christopher Landau met with Solomon Islands Prime Minister Matthew Wale to discuss ways to strengthen and deepen the U.S.- Solomon Islands bilateral relationship.  Deputy Secretary Landau and Prime Minister Wale signed a Letter of Intent to return Peace Corps to Solomon Islands.  Deputy Secretary Landau highlighted the new Development Finance Corporation Investment Initiative Agreement with Solomon Islands as well as the recent success with the Millennium Challenge Corporation’s Threshold Program.  He also announced the State Department is providing $6 million in new funding to expand its unexploded ordnance removal program in Solomon Islands.  Deputy Secretary Landau expressed his hope to visit Solomon Islands and to see the reminders of our shared sacrifices during World War II.

item.dc:creator: Office of the Spokesperson
item.description:
Office of the Spokesperson

Media Logistics for the G20 Foreign Ministers’ Meeting in Atlanta, Georgia

Media Note

July 21, 2026

Secretary of State Marco Rubio will host the G20 Foreign Ministers’ Meeting in Atlanta, Georgia, on Friday, October 30, 2026, and Saturday, October 31, 2026, bringing together foreign ministers and senior officials from the world’s leading economies to advance shared priorities focused on economic prosperity, energy security, and technological innovation.

Media interested in covering the G20 Foreign Ministerial Meetings may apply for credentials no later than August 21, 2026.

Approved media will receive confirmation with details regarding credential pick-up, security procedures, media access locations, camera positions, parking, and road closures. Additional logistical and operational details will be distributed to approved media closer to the event dates. Credentials are non-transferable.

For more information, visit the G20 website.
